priority: whether upper leaves are connate across the node
study_strategy.warning: Flower color alone is weak. Start with growth form, flower size, and leaf-node structure; use habitat only after morphology.

quick_key.if: low woody/subshrub habit in limestone cracks; thick leathery coarsely toothed leaves; red tubular flowers
very large pale lavender-to-white flowers about 35–55 mm; opposite serrate leaves sessile and often fused across node
glossy dark-green leaves and narrower pink-to-red flowers about 25–35 mm; Hill Country perennial
small lavender-violet flowers about 10–14 mm on slender branched stems in wet alluvial/coastal settings; sharply pointed calyx lobes

look_here_first: Start with growth form and flower SIZE, then photograph an opposite leaf node and a side-on blossom. Low woody stems in limestone with leathery toothed leaves and red tubes → P. baccharifolius. Very large pale lavender/white throat and sometimes connected upper leaves → P. cobaea. Narrower pink-red tubes and glossy leaves → P. triflorus. Small lavender flowers in wetter habitats → P. tenuis, a learner-only RANGE HOLD: do not count as verified native target-zone PASS.

shared_structure.recognition: Opposite leaves, bilaterally symmetrical tubular corollas usually with five spreading lobes, four fertile stamens and a fifth often hairy sterile STAMINODE ('beardtongue'); fruit a dry capsule with many seeds.
shared_structure.plain_terms: STAMINODE = sterile modified stamen often bearing hairs inside throat; CONNATE = two opposite leaves joined around stem; COROLLA THROAT = widened opening of fused petals; CALYX = sepals around flower base; DEHISCENT CAPSULE = dry fruit that splits open to shed seeds.
shared_structure.photo_tip: Front view of corolla alone rarely reveals staminode, calyx or joined leaf bases. Use front, strict side, and upper-node shots.
